supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:57 UTC, sam.okafor authenticated to WS-ICHEN-01 with a type-3 network logon from WS-SOKAFOR-01, source IP 10.40.10.23, receiving logon ID 0x9ab2f6f.
At 13:42:01 UTC, PowerShell PID 4720 ran as NWD\sam.okafor in that same logon session, executing powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \\FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1.

The administrator identity, originating workstation, script path, and business-hours timing match the workstation-patching practice supplied in the environment context. This supports an authorized-maintenance explanation for the alerted PowerShell activity.

PowerShell PID 4720 connected to 10.40.20.30:8080. Contemporaneous proxy telemetry reports a successful tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com with 38,800,000 server-to-client bytes; connection telemetry records a similar inbound volume.

PowerShell spawned wusa.exe to process C:\Windows\Temp\patches\windows11-kb5047001-x64.msu with /quiet /norestart. PowerShell terminated at 13:42:47 UTC, approximately 46 seconds after starting, consistent with the reported brief window.

known_telemetry_limitations: Process records identify the script path and installer command but do not expose script contents, package integrity, or installation results (T044-00084, T044-00090, T044-00092).

The Windows Update proxy record describes a CONNECT tunnel rather than decrypted payload contents and lacks a client source port; association with PowerShell is supported by timing and matching traffic volume rather than a shared proxy connection identifier (T044-00086 through T044-00089).
claims_not_established: Successful patch installation is not established by the installer launch and termination records (T044-00090 through T044-00093).
The records do not directly establish that the logged PowerShell process was the exact window the user saw, although its timing and short lifetime support that explanation (T044-00084, T044-00095).
unrelated_findings: Separate policy-review ticket: ivy.chen launched Firefox to https://customer.cloud.com/Citrix/StoreWeb/ and retrieved the portal and resource-list endpoint. This is outside the approved remote-access services described in the inventory; these records do not establish a remote session or a connection to the earlier PowerShell activity (T044-00163, T044-00172, T044-00189).

Separate process-review ticket: Webex.exe launched under ivy.chen with an app.slack.com URL, an unusual application/URL pairing. A loaded WebexHost.dll had a valid Cisco signature, but this does not establish the executable's integrity or maliciousness (T044-00168 through T044-00170).

Separate network-review ticket: DC-NWD-01 attempted connections to WS-ICHEN-01 on ports 8080, 443, 445, and 135 around 13:51 UTC. Connection records show REJ or S0 states and zero payload bytes; they do not establish successful remote administration or a relationship to the alerted PowerShell execution (T044-00127 through T044-00134).
